page: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio within an entry-level footprint. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled on an Intel Xeon processor. The CPU operates at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz and includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. The architecture supports modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core allocation ratio. The server includes no bundled local disk storage, instead utilizing remote storage options compatible with Azure Premium Storage volumes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-core computation alongside constrained multi-core throughput dictated by the 2 vCPU limit. The instance attained average scores on stress-ng single-core (1904.76) and Geekbench single-core (1943.0), as well as text processing (1810.0). However, parallel execution benchmarks place it lower in comparison groups, registering 1962.27 on multi-core stress-ng, 2182.0 on multi-core Geekbench, and 3670.32 on the PassMark CPU test. In-memory data store evaluations showed 2.58 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the instance is targeted at memory-bound tasks rather than parallel compute workloads. The dense 8 GB per vCPU distribution is suited for low-concurrency databases, small in-memory caching tiers, microservices requiring significant memory overhead, and development or staging environments.
description: Microsoft Azure EC2es_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for workloads requiring an elevated memory footprint within a dual-vCPU footprint. Driven by an Intel Xeon TDX processor clocked up to 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 2 vCPUs from a single hyper-threaded physical core, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory and 260 MB of L3 cache. The CPU features extensive instruction support, including AVX-512, Intel AMX, and accelerated cryptography. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage via premium disks, and does not include GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight capable single-threaded processing alongside predictable multi-core limitations typical of small core counts, with Redis SET operations achieving 2.58 million operations per second. This hardware profile suits low-traffic database engines, caching layers, and lightweight memory-dependent services.
